change: Discover managed pools through fallible fresh read-only open, preserve explicit/observed GC requirements across Config clones, reread the shared requirement after probing, and never recreate an auto-discovered missing catalog. Prevent successful no-op retain after stale/erroring stat and resulting acknowledged-data loss.
api_change: Rust Config::gc_enabled now returns Result<bool>; Python signatures are unchanged.

verification.baseline_public_regressions: Both added Python tests fail against the previous wheel: known catalog disappears; cold lookup returns ELOOP. Both pass on the new wheel.
verification.prior_82_tlc_algorithm_config_and_state_: unchanged; EnvironmentCatalog additionally defines discovery response domains

scope.rust: Verus proves the actual discovery decision function for all explicit/remembered/observation inputs. Shared atomic state, memory ordering, File::open, I/O error classification and full Config/Coordinator/GC composition remain unproved. The 73 count includes derived methods, not 73 APIs.
scope.tla: Separate finite discovery, acknowledged ownership handoff and deletion model. Retain is atomic and durable; no byte-level replay/lock/ownership refinement. Four positive configurations check all invariants and conditional termination. Three algorithm negatives and one environment-only negative select TypeOK and NoLostAcknowledgedData to reach actual deletion beyond the earlier ownership violation.
scope.environment: ENV-GC-DISCOVERY requires managed/legacy pool mode established before participants operate and trustworthy initial fresh-open NotFound. False initial open absence still gives a counterexample; live legacy-to-GC migration is excluded. Explicit online_gc=True avoids deciding legacy from initial absence, but does not prove the remaining I/O/locking contracts.
scope.faults: Private exact-path LD_PRELOAD injections only; not evidence of naturally occurring JuiceFS faults. New code avoids stat discovery, so all 160 armed fixed stat faults are unused. Separate 40 fresh-open EIO injections are consumed, return failure before acknowledgement, preserve the source owner, and succeed on retry.
scope.timing: Each fixed scenario has 40 first-retain samples; nearest-rank p99 equals the maximum. Four stat-labelled groups measure successful retains with unused stat faults. The open-error group measures failed return, not a successful retain. No latency guarantee or retry/time-out spec is inferred. The 276.66 ms untraced sample is unattributed.
scope.limits: This is a 2 KiB publication correctness campaign, not a 100 GB/TB bandwidth rerun. Earlier bandwidth measurements, binaries and untraced tail-latency anomalies remain separately scoped.

measurement.scope: Four hosts, private native 2 KiB publications, managed pool established before default-config destination clients. Cold/warm stat ENOENT/EIO are armed; new discovery avoids those syscalls, so these faults remain unused. Separate fixed cold read-only open EIO rejects before acknowledgement, preserves source, then succeeds on retry. Initial open NotFound and live legacy-to-managed migration are excluded. First-retain timings distinguish failed open from successful adoption; baseline false-success timing is not a performance baseline.
